fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the street.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can locate it without delay.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles so responding units can pull in and turn around without obstruction.
• Identify and mark a secondary access point through the perimeter fencing to give responders a direct path to the rear of the property.
• Keep any gate providing rear access unlocked or secured with a lockbox to avoid delays reaching the back of the property.
• Trim dense vegetation along walkways so responders can move between the main residence and detached structure without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation that crowds the path between the main residence and detached structure so both buildings are reachable on foot.
• Keep a clear path along the perimeter fencing so responders can move around the property without pushing through overgrown areas.
• Mark the water feature with a visible indicator so responders moving quickly across the lawn at night do not step into it.
• Identify a flat, open area near the driveway that can serve as a staging area for equipment and personnel.
• Post a simple site diagram near the front entrance showing the location of the detached structure, rear access point, and water feature.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing close to the structure on any side where vegetation is visibly touching or within a few feet of walls or foundation.
• Thin scattered shrubs in the grass-covered areas nearest the structure to break up continuous patches of vegetation leading toward the building.
• Mow or cut grass close to the structure, particularly during dry periods when standing grass is most likely to carry fire.
• Remove any dead grass, dry plant material, or accumulated debris from around the base of the structure.
• Keep tree branches trimmed up from the ground so low limbs do not connect ground-level vegetation to the tree canopy.
• Thin shrubs between scattered trees and the structure to reduce the amount of connected vegetation that could carry fire toward the building.
• Clear any vegetation, branches, or debris from along the driveway to keep the single access route open for vehicles entering and exiting.
• Keep the driveway surface and shoulders clear of encroaching grass and shrubs that could narrow the travel lane.
• Clear vegetation from the rear of the property as much as possible to create usable space for movement around the structure, given that rear access is limited.
• Mark or keep clear the single access route so it remains easy to identify and navigate under poor visibility conditions.
• Keep the area around the water feature clear of overhanging branches and accumulated debris that could restrict access to it.
